title: fix: keep shared dialogs rounded on narrow screens
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Gives every dialog the same rounded, content-sized layout below 480px: full width, an 8px vertical gap, and edge-to-edge inner cards. Larger screens retain a 16px inset.
- Removes the mobile-width opt-out, including confirmation and key-created exceptions. Keeps expandable forms top-aligned and completed results centered; preserves Economics document-preview height.
- Preserves button semantics: server writes are outlined; navigation and export actions, including device Continue and Copy and close, retain the default filled style.
- Preserves the dedicated payment footer, ordinary Button defaults, and scrollbar styles. Related viewport work: #15786.

Validation:
- 93 UI tests; UI, Enter, and Economics typechecks; Enter frontend and Economics builds; Biome and diff checks.
- 320 Chromium/WebKit layout checks; 40 light/dark footer comparisons, refreshed after restoring the navigation/export styles. Expansion, cancel, Escape, focus, and local auth-error checks passed.

Local previews use real components with sample props and label illustrative authorization, device, and payment layouts. These verify presentation, not authenticated payments or account mutations.

gist.headline: Round corners, small screens
gist.blurb: Dialogs keep their rounded corners on narrow screens. The cards fit, and the buttons still know what they do.
gist.summary: Shared dialogs below 480px get rounded, content-sized, full-width layouts with an 8px vertical gap and edge-to-edge inner cards; larger screens retain their 16px inset.
gist.impact: Confirmation, API-key, resource, and Economics dialogs fit consistently on phones while preserving form and result alignment, document-preview height, and distinct button styles for writes versus navigation and export.
gist.visual_concept: Show a small phone with a neatly rounded dialog and a wider monitor with an inset dialog, making the responsive layout change legible. Polli, wearing a tiny tailor's measuring tape, adjusts the phone dialog's corners beside a little code-plant.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel art workspace, Polli uses a tiny tailor's measuring tape to straighten a rounded dialog on a phone, while a nearby monitor shows the roomier version and a code-plant grows between them. Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes; use a prominent soft lime green (#ecf874) glow and dark purple (#110518) outlines.
